lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: would probably pass (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: Doesn't apply: banks and finance companies don't split their balance sheet into current and non-current.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.w: Doesn't apply: borrowing is the raw material of a lender's business.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years

ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: A gap of about 24 months without a dividend (2019-07 to 2021-07).

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years

ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +33%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings

story.what_it_does: ICICI Bank is an Indian bank that takes deposits and makes loans, earning mostly from the gap between the two. In FY2026 it earned a profit after tax of ₹501.47 billion, with loans up 15.8% and deposits up 11.4%.
story.plans: Management expects net interest margin to be range-bound in FY27 but gave no loan growth number or target. It also expects to update on the agri standard asset provision and to deploy excess liquidity within two quarters, and it aims for carbon neutrality for Scope 1 and 2 emissions by fiscal 2032.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a competitive moat directly. They show signs of strength: low net bad loans (0.30% at Sep-26), capital adequacy of 16.68%, and loan and deposit growth that has accelerated, with loans up 30.0% in Sep-26.

scenarios.story: Loan growth has accelerated from 15.8% in March 2026 to 30.0% in September 2026, and profit rose 20.1% in Q2 FY27 while net NPAs fell to 0.30%. Capital stays comfortable and excess liquidity is put to work.
signals_to_watch: Net NPA ratio staying near or below 0.30%
Profit after tax growth continuing after the 20.1% rise in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Growth stays strong and asset quality stable, but margin eases from 4.36% to 4.18% and management says deposit repricing will bring only moderate increases. Management calls the margin dip optical and expects NIM to be range-bound in FY27.
signals_to_watch: Net interest margin versus the 4.18% in Q2 FY27
Cost of deposits versus the 4.50% in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: The RBI-directed agri provision (₹12.83 bn), a ₹20,000-25,000 crore portfolio that needs repair, could hit future earnings. The credit card book keeps shrinking, treasury income turned negative, and the West Asia conflict adds uncertainty to credit demand and asset quality.
signals_to_watch: Update on the agri standard asset provision in the next two quarters
Credit card book decline (down 9.7% year on year in Sep-26)
